description:
Receiver typed atom (or any): the call dispatches over the modules a value can name that define f/n; a miss raises UndefinedFunctionError (rescuable), a non-atom raises ArgumentError with Elixir's text.

Settled design (probed before building):

- Candidate set. World::nameable_modules is one monotone set: every module whose source the compile has indexed, and every module a lowered body writes as a value (alias, struct). It is the unit fact FactKey::NameableModules, read by the call whether or not it holds anything yet. 'Every library module' was rejected by measurement: requiring all 24 top-level lib modules takes hello world from 213 jobs to 342.
- Filter. nameable_module_callees waits on ModuleDefined for each candidate and reads its ModuleInterface. DefineModule is a scope walk and compiles no body, so the filter demands DefineModule and never DefineFunction.
- Miss. The miss is one more target of the callsite: SelectedCallee::Undefined(UndefinedFunction), selected by the receiver's type less the candidates' atoms, with no activation and return type none. It flows through call_destinations unchanged and materializes as CallTarget::Undefined. Native ends the arm in Term::RaiseUndefined (fz_raise_undefined_function); the interpreter calls failure::raise_undefined_function.
- A receiver that is never an atom (fixture 00866) stays the compile refusal type/module-value-call. A receiver whose type lists its atoms resolves each at compile time as before; anything else in the type goes to the miss.

Trace: hello world stays at 213 jobs (5 IndexCode, 14 DefineModule).

Fixtures: 00867 (an atom made at run time calls the module it names; replaces the refusal of that number), 00869 (every miss, worded as Elixir words it). 00866 stays.

Known differences from Elixir, documented in .agent/docs/modules.md: a module in a library file the compile never indexed and no body names is 'not available' to a computed atom; m.f() with no arguments on a map raises ArgumentError where Elixir reads the field and warns.
title: A call on a plain-atom receiver dispatches over the modules the program can name
